AWARD 1.

Vide this order I shall dispose off the 'Detailed Accident Report' (hereinafter referred to as 'DAR')
filed by the police with regard to road traffic accident occurred on 15.01.2020 in which injured namely Amit Chauhan (hereinafter referred to as 'petitioner') suffered injuries.

Copy of DAR was supplied to the petitioner as well as to Gajender Singh (hereinafter referred to as respondent No. 1),
Narender (hereinafter referred to as respondent No. 2), who are the driver and registered owner of the vehicle involved in the accident i.e. truck bearing registration no. HR46E 0349 (hereinafter referred to as 'vehicle in question').

The copy of the DAR was also supplied to the Ld. Counsel for the Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 3), as the vehicle in question was duly insured with it as on the date of accident.

2. In brief, the facts of the case are that during the investigation, the IO recorded the statement of eye-witness namely Rahul Kumar under Section 161 CrPC, as under: -
"
On 15/01/2020, I was coming from Alipur in my car after selling vegetables from GT Karnal Road with my mother Shanichari Kuvar.
I went a little ahead from the Livaspur Under Pass and turned my car to the left towards Swarup Nagar and was going towards Livaspur Under Pass.

As soon as I reached near the police picket at around 11:45 PM, a motorcyclist came from behind from the Livaspur side and at the same time, truck no. HR 46 E 0349, driven by its driver at a high speed and carelessly and hit the motorcyclist due to which the motorcyclist fell down and the truck driver dragged him away.
Other people also came there.
The truck driver stopped his truck at some distance due to the crowd and with the help of my mother I tried to catch the truck driver but the truck driver escaped"

3. It is further matter of record that a criminal case vide FIR No. 36/20 under Section 279/338 IPC was registered in PS Swaroop Nagar and charge sheet under Section 173 Cr.PC under the above FIR was filed against respondent no.1 / driver of the vehicle in question for causing the accident.
4. Respondent.

no. 1 and 2 have filed their joint written statement stating that respondent no. 1 was driving his vehicle with due care and diligence by obeying all the traffic rules and regulations and accident had occurred as the petitioner was driving his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and he himself lost control over the motorcycle and met with accident.

It is further stated that respondent no. 1 was having valid driving licence and vehicle of respondent no. 2 was duly insured with respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. and hence liability to pay compensation is of respondent no. 3 / Ins.
Co.

3

5. Respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has not disputed the accident and has filed legal offer of Rs. 47,748/-
after deducting 20% contributory negligence but the offer was not acceptable to the petitioner.

6. After completion of the pleadings following issues were framed vide order dated 19.07.2022: -
1.
Whether the offer / compensation made by the respondent no. 3 is reasonable and if not so, what amount petitioner is entitled for?

OPP.
2. Relief.
7.
In order to prove the claim, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and filed his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A.
None from the respondents opted to lead any evidence.
Accordingly, RE was closed vide order dated 23.07.2025.
8. I have heard ld. counsels appearing on behalf of petitioner and respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. and gone through the record carefully.
None has appeared on behalf of the respondents no. 1 and 2 for advancing final argument either through video conference or in person.
9. My issue-wise findings are as under:-
ISSUE No.1
Whether the offer / compensation made by the respondent no. 3 is reasonable and if not so, what amount petitioner is entitled for?
OPP. No issue with regard to negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 was framed, as respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has not disputed the accident and even filed the offer.

However, before petitioner is held to be entitled for any compensation he has to prove that he suffered injuries in this accident on account of rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 and to prove the same, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex
. PW1/A.

Petitioner / PW1 deposed that on 15.01.2020,
he was coming to his home on his Bullet Motorcycle DL11SW6361 after finishing his duty at his work place at Sector-16, Rohini and at about 11.15 p. m, when he reached near police pocket, Libaspur, under pass towards Swaroop Nagar, a truck bearing no HR46E0349 driven at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner came from the side of Nagli Poona at service road and hit his motorcycle and due to which he fell down and received grievous multiple injuries Though, petitioner / PW1 has been cross examined by the respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. but nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1, with regard to rash and negligent driving by respondent no. 1, as petitioner being injured is natural eye- witness of accident and petitioner/PW1 has not at all been cross examined by the respondent no. 1 on the aspect of manner in which the accident had occurred.

Further, respondent no. 1, being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner, the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence and there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case,
Amit Chauhan vs Gajender Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56101662/
4 meaning thereby that respondent no. 1 has nothing to say about the rash and negligence and the manner in which the accident had occurred.
Further, the DAR collectively Ex. PW1/1 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by his MLC filed along with the DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Further, there is nothing on record which shows that respondent no. 1 has ever approached to any higher authority against his false implication in the present case.

Relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs.
Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under:-
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.

Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs.
Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident claim applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that petitioner suffered grievous injuries in a vehicular accident caused by the respondent no. 1 while driving the vehicle in question in rash and negligent manner and being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.

Now, coming to the issue with respect to the quantum of compensation and below are the finding: -
10.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009),
held as under:
"Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not intended to be a bonanza, largesse or source of profit".

11. It is deposed by PW1 / petitioner he was working as salesman and earing Rs. 16,000/- per month and after the accident he is unable to work and suffered financial loss on account of staple diet, loss of earning, transportation & attendance etc. and claimed compensation of Rs. 50,00,000/-

The Original medical bills amounting to Rs4,34,336/- filed and proved on record, duly verified by the counsel for petitioner and there is no rebuttal evidence with regard to the original medical bills.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs. 4,34,336/- is allowed to the petitioner against the original medical bills.
Though, except deposition of petitioner, there is no evidence to verify that any amount has been spent on special diet and conveyance etc.

However, keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period of his hospitalization as well as the surgeries and procedures Amit Chauhan vs Gajender Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56101662/
5 undergone by him and the record of his follow up treatment, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner must have incurred expenses on special diet required for his speedy recovery and conveyance.
Accordingly, Rs.20,000/- each towards special diet and conveyance are awarded to the petitioner.

12. It is a matter of record that during the pendency of the case, the petitioner was referred to Dr.
BSA Hospital for assessment of permanent disability and a certificate received on record, as per which petitioner has suffered 76% permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb.

Since the permanent disability of petitioner has been assessed by the government hospital / disability board,
this Tribunal has no reason to disbelieve the disability certificate received on record.

13. As far as loss of income on account of loss of future earning due to disability is concerned,
petitioner as PW1 has deposed that he was working as a salesman and earning Rs. 16,000/- per month but admittedly there is no document to prove the contention except deposition of petitioner.
Hence, the income of petitioner could not be proved on record and no document with regard to education qualification of petitioner has been filed on record.

During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for petitioner submitted that since the petitioner has suffered permanent disability, loss to future income may be calculated as per Minimum Wages Act, prevalent at the time of accident.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that petitioner has suffered 76%
permanent disability in relation to left lower limb, which is permanent in nature and following the principles of justice, equity and good conscience and to adopt more realistic, pragmatic and liberal approach, the Tribunal is of the view that loss to future income has to be assessed while taking the income under Minimum Wages Act applicable in Delhi State to unskilled person in the absence of education qualification documents.
The minimum wages of unskilled person were Rs.14,842/- at the time of accident in Delhi.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs.14,842/-/- is taken for calculating loss to future income.

14. As far as loss of income during the treatment is concerned, as stated above petitioner has suffered 76% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb and considering the same, it is presumed that petitioner would have not been able to continue his work for about 12 months.

Accordingly, Rs 1,78,104/- (14,842x12) is awarded to the petitioner towards loss of income during the period of his treatment and during this period he must have taken the services of an attendant and hence a sum of Rs.60,000/- (5000x12) for three months towards attendant charges are also awarded to the petitioner.
15.

As far as loss of income on account of loss of future earning due to disability is concerned, there is no dispute with regard to the disability suffered by the petitioner and no rebuttal evidence has brought on record with regard to the disability certificate and hence considering the 76% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb, the functional disability is taken as 38% qua whole body for calculating the loss of earning capacity, as there is no doubt, this kind of disability would hamper his day to day activity and work for gain.

16. As per photocopy of Aadhar card of petitioner filed on record, his date of birth is 16.10.1987,
which inter alias means that petitioner was 32 years and 2 months in age at the time of accident and Amit Chauhan vs Gajender Singh on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56101662/
6 hence a multiplier of 16 (as per the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sarla Verma vs Delhi Transport Corporation, 2009 ACJ 1298) is taken for calculating his loss to future earnings.

Counting in this way,
his loss to future earnings, comes to Rs. 15,16,021.24p, details of which are well mentioned in the attached proforma.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs. 15,16,021.24p, is allowed to petitioner, as loss of future earnings, due to permanent disability.
No tax is deducted since the said income of petitioner is not taxable.
17. Further, apart from the above mentioned amounts, petitioner is entitled for compensation regarding mental pain and suffering, disfiguration, marriage prospects etc.

Accordingly, after giving due weight-age to the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- for mental pain and physical shock as well as for pain and suffering due to this accident, Rs.1,00,000/-
towards loss of amenities of life, Rs. 1,00,000/- for disfiguration Rs.1,00,000/- for loss of inconvenience, hardship disappointment, frustration, mention stress dejectment and unhappiness in future life etc. are also awarded to the petitioner, making a total sum of Rs. 26,28,461.24p, details of which is mentioned in the attached proforma.

In the light of the above discussion, the aspect of liability of the respondent is to be adjudicated and findings are mentioned below: -
18.
Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.

However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical pleas and during the arguments ld. Counsel for Ins. Co. stated that the accident is head on collusion and hence some contributory negligence may be attributed on the part of petitioner himself.
Going through the, cross examination of PW1 / petitioner, it is found that petitioner has denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to his negligence.

Further, PW1 / petitioner has not at all been cross examined by the respondent on 1 on this aspect to prove that there is any contributory negligence on the part of petitioner nor respondent no. 1 examined himself.

Further,
Ins. Co. has not examined witness nor any document has been placed on record to support the contention that accident was head on collusion or that there is any contributory negligence on the part of petitioner.
Admittedly respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and even filed legal offer.

The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue has not led any evidence on such aspect.
Hence, merely taking the plea, insurance company cannot escape from its liabilities.
In view of the above and since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner / insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Issue no. 1 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co.
holding that petitioner is entitled to get award amount as compensation from respondent no.3 / Ins.
Co.

As far as loss of income on account of loss of future earning due to disability is concerned, there is no dispute with regard to the disability suffered by the petitioner and no rebuttal evidence has brought on record with regard to the disability certificate and hence considering the 76% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb, the functional disability is taken as 38% qua whole body for calculating the loss of earning capacity, as there is no doubt, this kind of disability would hamper his day to day activity and work for gain.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs. 15,16,021.24p, is allowed to petitioner, as loss of future earnings, due to permanent disability.
No tax is deducted since the said income of petitioner is not taxable.
17. Further, apart from the above mentioned amounts, petitioner is entitled for compensation regarding mental pain and suffering, disfiguration, marriage prospects etc.
Admittedly respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has no statutory defence and even filed legal offer.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue has not led any evidence on such aspect.
Hence, merely taking the plea, insurance company cannot escape from its liabilities.
In view of the above and since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner / insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.
